smell_validity.evidence: Feature envy is real where Debouncer::backlog_report and the remove_root gauge dissect DebounceDataInner's queues, rename/rescan events, errors, roots through the lock, and explain_raw_event renders the shared-crate Event. But trace_watches and trace_content_aliases own the tables they read, so envy reaches only the entry records there, blurring the boundary from reasonable design into a mixed-strength story.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Rendering rules for DebounceDataInner's internals sit on the facade and cleanup path, so future changes to queue, rename/rescan or error bookkeeping require synchronized edits in Debouncer, and later diagnostics risk copying the misplaced shape. The gain is real but bounded: these are read-only observability renderers, so the burden is error-prone diagnostic maintenance rather than delivery-behavior damage.

development_plausibility.evidence: Triage-driven trace helpers placed at trigger sites fit notify's existing log::trace usage, real field vocabulary (EventKind, attrs, watch masks/descriptors, NANOS_PER_SECOND granularity) and plausible support-thread comments. The code reads as organic repository work; the batch-wide repetition of five same-shaped string renderers in one release window adds slight task-shaped regularity, keeping it below reference authenticity.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt converts an ambiguous refactor into a reliable contract: it enumerates every batch site via the four threads plus an explicit batch-wide scope rule, fixes the finished state (behavior homed on the data it describes, call sites just request the account), and materially de-risks wrong direction and partial cleanup with an exact output-diff oracle, preserved public callability/docs, untouched behavior and tests, and a leave-well-placed-be exclusion, while leaving implementation shape open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: At least four distinct purposes: public report delegation, an inline gauge extracted while the write lock is held, cross-crate rehoming onto the shared Event type, and two table renderers needing entry-versus-summary or pairwise-rule placement decisions. These require different placement, visibility and granularity decisions; only the two debouncer-full sites share one rehoming rule.

localization_burden.evidence: Scope is essentially fully described: the four threads cover all five helpers findable via local call chains (unwatch into remove_root, the watch-install loop, the poll rescan) and content-matched searches across four files in three crates. Each site is then judged against its own record ownership without combining other components' behavior or excluding alias-registered decoys.

repair_coordination.evidence: Each site can be repaired independently; no shared cross-site rule breaks behaviorally if one differs. Coordination is limited to propagation when each new renderer home meets its caller: method signatures, visibility (including the cross-crate Event surface) and delegates preserving identical outputs.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform rule — rehome the string assembly onto the primary record it reads, with the caller asking for text — cleanly covers backlog_report, the remove_root gauge (same DebounceDataInner owner) and the cross-crate explain_raw_event, roughly 60% of locations. trace_watches already receives its own table, and trace_content_aliases needs pairwise PathData comparison, so each requires a separate split decision a uniform move cannot make.

behavioral_risk.evidence: All injected behavior is either trace-gated or a brand-new unchecked public String method, so drift like a dropped branch, changed firing situation, or an orphan-gauge miscomputation compiles and passes the untouched suite. A concrete near-miss — routing the remove_root gauge through a lock-taking helper — deadlocks only when unwatch runs with trace enabled, a state combination no assertion observes.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
